statement: If from a medial straight line there be subtracted a medial straight line which is commensurable with the whole in square only, and which contains with the whole a medial rectangle, the remainder is irrational; and let it be called a second apotome of a medial straight line.
heath_proof: For from the medial straight line AB let there be subtracted the medial straight line CB which is commensurable with the whole AB in square only and such that the rectangle AB, BC, which it contains with the whole AB, is medial; [X. 28] I say that the remainder AC is irrational; and let it be called a second apotome of a medial straight line. For let a rational straight line DI be set out, let DE equal to the squares on AB, BC be applied to DI, producing DG as breadth, and let DH equal to twice the rectangle AB, BC be applied to DI, producing DF as breadth; therefore the remainder FE is equal to the square on AC. [II. 7] Now, since the squares on AB, BC are medial and commensurable, therefore DE is also medial. [X. 15 and 23] And it is applied to the rational straight line DI, producing DG as breadth; therefore DG is rational and incommensurable in length with DI. [X. 22] Again, since the rectangle AB, BC is medial, therefore twice the rectangle AB, BC is also medial. [X. 23] And it is equal to DH; therefore DH is also medial. And it has been applied to the rational straight line DI, producing DF as breadth; therefore DF is rational and incommensurable in length with DI. [X. 22] And, since AB, BC are commensurable in square only, therefore AB is incommensurable in length with BC; therefore the square on AB is also incommensurable with the rectangle AB, BC. [X. 11] But the squares on AB, BC are commensurable with the square on AB, [X. 15] and twice the rectangle AB, BC is commensurable with the rectangle AB, BC; [X. 6] therefore twice the rectangle AB, BC is incommensurable with the squares on AB, BC. [X. 13] But DE is equal to the squares on AB, BC, and DH to twice the rectangle AB, BC; therefore DE is incommensurable with DH. But, as DE is to DH, so is GD to DF; [VI. 1] therefore GD is incommensurable with DF. [X. 11] And both are rational; therefore GD, DF are rational straight lines commensurable in square only; therefore FG is an apotome. [X. 73] But DI is rational, and the rectangle contained by a rational and an irrational straight line is irrational, [deduction from X. 20] and its ’side’ is irrational. And AC is the ’side’ of FE; therefore AC is irrational. And let it be called a second apotome of a medial straight line.

**Statement.** If from a medial straight line there be subtracted a medial straight line which is commensurable with the whole in square only, and which contains with the whole a medial rectangle, the remainder is irrational; and let it be called a second apotome of a medial straight line.

**Setting out.** Let AB be a medial straight line, and from AB let there be subtracted the medial straight line BC, which is commensurable with the whole AB in square only and is such that the rectangle AB, BC contained by it with the whole is medial. I say that the remainder AC is irrational.

**Step 1.** Let a rational straight line DI be set out (D10.1.3). To DI let there be applied the rectangle DE equal to the squares on AB, BC, producing DG as breadth; and to DI let there be applied the rectangle DH equal to twice the rectangle AB, BC, producing DF as breadth, F being taken on the line DG (1.44).

**Step 2.** Since the straight line AB is cut at C, the squares on AB, BC together are equal to twice the rectangle AB, BC together with the square on AC (2.7). Hence DE is equal to DH together with the square on AC. Therefore DE is greater than DH (CN5), so that DF is less than DG and F falls between D and G; and, subtracting DH from DE, the remainder FE is equal to the square on AC (CN3).

**Step 3.** Since AB, BC are commensurable in square, the square on AB is commensurable with the square on BC (D10.1.2). Therefore the sum of the squares on AB, BC is commensurable with the square on AB (10.15). But the square on AB is a medial area, being the square on the medial straight line AB; and an area commensurable with a medial area is medial (Porism to 10.23). Therefore DE, which is equal to the squares on AB, BC, is medial, that is, DE is equal to the square on a medial straight line.

**Step 4.** DE is the square on a medial straight line applied to the rational straight line DI, producing DG as breadth; therefore DG is rational and incommensurable in length with DI (10.22).

**Step 5.** The rectangle AB, BC is medial by hypothesis. Twice the rectangle AB, BC has to the rectangle AB, BC the ratio which the number 2 has to the number 1; therefore twice the rectangle AB, BC is commensurable with the rectangle AB, BC (10.6). Hence twice the rectangle AB, BC, and therefore DH which is equal to it, is medial (Porism to 10.23). DH is thus the square on a medial straight line applied to the rational straight line DI, producing DF as breadth; therefore DF is rational and incommensurable in length with DI (10.22).

**Step 6.** Since AB, BC are commensurable in square only, AB is incommensurable in length with BC. Now the square on AB and the rectangle AB, BC are parallelograms under the same height AB, standing on the bases AB and BC respectively; therefore, as AB is to BC, so is the square on AB to the rectangle AB, BC (6.1). Since AB is incommensurable with BC, the square on AB is incommensurable with the rectangle AB, BC (10.11).

**Step 7.** The sum of the squares on AB, BC is commensurable with the square on AB (Step 3), and the square on AB is incommensurable with the rectangle AB, BC (Step 6); therefore the sum of the squares on AB, BC is incommensurable with the rectangle AB, BC (10.13). Again, twice the rectangle AB, BC is commensurable with the rectangle AB, BC (Step 5), and the rectangle AB, BC is incommensurable with the sum of the squares on AB, BC; therefore twice the rectangle AB, BC is incommensurable with the sum of the squares on AB, BC (10.13). That is, DH is incommensurable with DE.

**Step 8.** DE and DH are parallelograms under the same height DI, standing on the bases DG and DF; therefore, as DE is to DH, so is DG to DF (6.1). Since DE is incommensurable with DH, DG is incommensurable in length with DF (10.11).

**Step 9.** DG is rational and incommensurable in length with DI (Step 4); hence DG is commensurable with DI in square only (D10.1.3), so that the square on DG is commensurable with the square on DI. Likewise DF is rational and incommensurable in length with DI (Step 5), so that the square on DF is commensurable with the square on DI. Therefore the square on DG is commensurable with the square on DF (10.12), that is, DG and DF are commensurable in square (D10.1.2). Together with Step 8, DG and DF are rational straight lines commensurable in square only.

**Step 10.** DF is less than DG (Step 2), and from the rational straight line DG there has been subtracted the rational straight line DF commensurable with DG in square only; therefore the remainder FG is an apotome, and it is irrational (10.73).

**Step 11.** The rectangle FE is contained by FG and FH, where FH is equal to the rational straight line DI; that is, FE is an area applied to the rational straight line DI with FG as breadth. If FE were a rational area, then, being applied to the rational straight line DI, it would produce as breadth a straight line rational and commensurable in length with DI (10.20); but its breadth FG is irrational (Step 10). Therefore FE is not rational; that is, FE is an irrational area (D10.1.4).

**Step 12.** But FE is equal to the square on AC (Step 2). Therefore AC is the straight line on which is described a square equal to an irrational area; hence AC is irrational (D10.1.4).

**Conclusion.** Therefore, if from a medial straight line AB there be subtracted a medial straight line BC commensurable with the whole in square only and containing with the whole a medial rectangle, the remainder AC is irrational; and let it be called a second apotome of a medial straight line. Q.E.D.

**Path note.** The proof follows the application-of-areas route used for the additive irrationals (compare 10.38): the square on the remainder is exhibited as a rectangle under the rational line DI with an apotome as breadth, and 10.20 (contrapositive) then forces the area, and hence its side, to be irrational. The medial character of DE and DH is obtained from the Porism to 10.23 (an area commensurable with a medial area is medial) rather than by re-deriving it from 2.14 and 10.21, which is why 10.23 appears and 10.21 does not.
